title: Where can treasures be hidden so no jump size reaches both?
description: {{NAME_4}} hides two treasures and {{NAME_2}} picks one jump size, so the board lists the factors of each hiding number and looks for a shared jump size. Keeko doubts that twelve and twenty six are safe.
teaching_notes: One idea: a jump size reaches a number only if it is a factor of that number, so two numbers are safe when they share no factor other than one. Watch for students who judge safety by how the numbers look instead of listing their factors.

source: Treasures are on two numbers; {{NAME_2}} gets them only if he rea
video_script.why: The child sees that a jump size reaches a number only when it is a factor of that number, so a pair is safe when no allowed jump size is a factor of both.
video_script.substitution: List the factors of each treasure number and look for a jump size other than one that is in both lists.
video_script.anchor: A number line from 0 with a treasure on each of two numbers and a jumping frog
video_script.wrong_answer: twelve and twenty six are safe
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko thinks twelve and twenty six are safe because they look unrelated, but two divides both, so a jump size of two lands on both treasures.
video_script.payoff_line: Place them on numbers with no common factor other than one, such as four and nine.

final_answer.value: On two numbers with no common factor other than 1, e.g. 4 and 9
final_answer.spoken: numbers that share no jump size except one

names.{{NAME_2}}: picks one jump size and tries to reach both treasures

maths_rules: a jump size lands on a number exactly when it is a factor of that number
factors of 14: 1, 2, 7, 14; factors of 36: 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 9, 12, 18, 36; the shared factors are 1 and 2, so a jump of 2 reaches both
factors of 4: 1, 2, 4; factors of 9: 1, 3, 9; the only shared factor is 1, which is not allowed
12 = 2 × 6 and 26 = 2 × 13, so a jump of 2 reaches both 12 and 26
video_script.design: Two treasure chests sit on a number line; the factors of each hiding number are listed beside it and a shared jump size is highlighted in amber.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about the treasure game.
<bookmark mark='rule'/>{{NAME_4}} hides two treasures, and {{NAME_2}} picks one jump size and sticks to it.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Jump size one is not allowed. Where should {{NAME_4}} place the treasures so that {{NAME_2}} cannot reach both?

beats.on_screen: the number line and the chests stay on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a jump size reaches a number if it divides that number; reaching both needs a factor of both; safe = not reached by any jump size except 1

marks.jump: a jump of four lands on twelve and the frog stops
marks.both: two lists of factors are drawn with the shared jump sizes joined
marks.safe: the word safe appears beside a pair that no jump reaches

narration: <bookmark mark='jump'/>A jump size lands on a number when it divides that number exactly.
<bookmark mark='both'/>To reach both treasures, the jump size must be a factor of both numbers.
<bookmark mark='safe'/>A pair is safe when no allowed jump size reaches both.

beats.on_screen: Given: 2 treasures; 1 jump size for both; jump size 1 is not allowed
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, two treasures, one jump size for both, and no jump of size one.

beats.on_screen: To find: where to hide the treasures so no allowed jump reaches both

marks.find: the words to find are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to place the treasures so that no allowed jump reaches both.

marks.fourteen: the factors of fourteen are listed
marks.thirty: the factors of thirty six are listed and the shared two is highlighted in amber

narration: <bookmark mark='fourteen'/>Step one, try fourteen and thirty six. The factors of fourteen are one, two, seven and fourteen.
<bookmark mark='thirty'/>Thirty six has the factor two as well. A jump of two lands on both, and this pair is not safe.

marks.four: the factors of four are listed
marks.nine: the factors of nine are listed
marks.shared: only the jump size one is joined, and it is crossed out as not allowed

narration: <bookmark mark='four'/>Step two, try four and nine. The factors of four are one, two and four.
<bookmark mark='nine'/>The factors of nine are one, three and nine.
<bookmark mark='shared'/>Only one is shared, and a jump of one is not allowed.

beats.on_screen: Compare: 14 and 36 share 2 (reached); 4 and 9 share only 1 (safe)

marks.first: the first pair is marked reached
marks.second: the second pair is marked safe

narration: <bookmark mark='first'/>Step three, compare the two tries. Fourteen and thirty six share the jump size two, so {{NAME_2}} reaches both.
<bookmark mark='second'/>Four and nine share nothing but one, so no allowed jump reaches both.

beats.on_screen: Answer: numbers with no common factor other than 1, e.g. 4 and 9
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Place them on numbers with no common factor other than one, such as four and nine.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt: 12 and 26 are safe, crossed out; 12 = 2 × 6 and 26 = 2 × 13

marks.doubt: Keeko's doubt appears in a bubble
marks.reason: twelve and twenty six are written as two times six and two times thirteen

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks twelve and twenty six are safe, because they look unrelated.
<bookmark mark='reason'/>But two divides twelve, and two divides twenty six.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A jump of two lands on both, so looks do not decide it. Shared factors do.
